e7_s4_rationale: The presence of marked osteolysis and collapse of the T1 vertebra, along with the involvement of the anterior and posterior longitudinal ligaments, is consistent with a giant cell tumor. The tumor's location in the spine and its effects on the surrounding structures, including the nerves, also align with this diagnosis.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Chordoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Chordomas are typically midline and more commonly found in the clivus or sacrum

e7_s4_rejected.label: Osteolytic metastasis
e7_s4_rejected.why: Metastases are more common in older adults and would not typically cause such localized destruction without other systemic symptoms

e7_s4_rejected.label: Plasmacytoma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Plasmacytomas are typically associated with multiple myeloma and would likely have other systemic symptoms and findings

e7_s4_rejected.label: Multiple myeloma
e7_s4_rejected.why: Multiple myeloma would likely have other systemic symptoms, such as anemia, renal failure, and hypercalcemia, which are not mentioned in the vignette
